newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Paris plunges, dlr soars on French left win.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Paris plunges, dlr soars on French left win.

text.p: The Paris bourse plunged more than three percent at one point on Monday as investors took fright at the victory for the left in Sunday's election which left the Socialists relying on the Communists to form a government.
In currencies, the dollar soared to near four-week peaks against the mark and French franc in Europe, buoyed by renewed uncertainty over monetary union after the left's win.
Elsewhere in Europe, Frankfurt stocks were not affected by the French gloom, climbing over one percent in early trade, but London fell on profit-taking in the financial sector.

But most eyes were on the French markets where the blue-chip CAC-40 index plumetted 85.19 points to 2,498.75 within minutes of the opening as markets digested a "worst case scenario" for French markets in which the Socialist-led left would need the Communist Party to secure its parliamentary majority.
The bourse recovered about half its losses by late morning, but was expected to stay volatile ahead of an announcement by the new government on its policy direction and on the composition.
"This is pretty surprising," said one trader in Paris. "I don't know if we're going to go lower but the CAC is getting very, very cheap."
He said much of the pressure in pre-session trading was from "Anglo-Saxons" afraid of the presence of Communists in the combined left majority.

The big drop in Paris followed a 6.48 percent loss last week in the run-up to Sunday's poll. "One hundred points is a lot after last week's drop," one trader said. "Especially since last week's drop was made with the knowledge that the left would probably win."
Conglomerate Lagardere, down 7.6 percent, and defence electronics firm Thomson-CSF, down 6.9 percent, were the top CAC losers as privatisation stocks were the hardest hit.
In curency markets, the dollar was the darling on traders.

The dollar was supported against other European currencies by anxiety over the future of economic and monetary union (EMU) after Socialist leader and Prime Minister in-waiting Lionel Jospin said voters had demanded a reorientation on Europe.
Against the mark, the U.S. currency was 1.7182 in early trade compared to 1.7087 in late Europe on Friday. Against the franc, the dollar climbed to 5.8132 ,compared to 5.7990.

"It is the Socialists winning in a manner in which they will have to depend on the Communists, known EMU opponents, (that will boost the dollar)," said Ian Gunner, international economist at Chase Investment Bank.

"This (the election) has been the straw that has broken the camel's back, as it raises further uncertainty about European issues -- particularly those concerning EMU. That is why sterling and the dollar have done well over the last 24 hours," said Gunner.

Analysts said the left was also expected to adopt a looser interpretation on the Maastricht Treaty, paving the way for a softer euro at the outset, said analysts. A delay to EMU is also expected to buoy the mark, but a soft euro would depress it.

Victory for France's Socialists, seen as keen on Italy and Spain to be included among EMU's founding members, comes after German government's plans to revalue Bundesbank assets to try to qualify for EMU. This was seen as improving the odds of a broad-based EMU and a softer euro from the outset.

"The French election results have increased the prospect of a softer euro. That is clearly bad news for the deutschmark, and clearly the dollar has benefited," said Nick Stamenkovic, economist at DKB International.

In London commodity markets, robusta coffee futures tumbled in early trade with benchmark July opening a sharp $270 down at $2,200 per tonne as the market took a sharp reverse from last week's spectacular rally.

The slide followed a steep 12-percent fall in New York on Friday on frantic speculative selling. By 0850 GMT, the London first-month contract fell further by $330 to $2,140. This compares with last week's 20-month-peak of $2,670.
CURRENCIES AT 0900 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.7182 marks and 116.32 yen compared with 1.7075 marks and 116. 37 yen in late European trading on Friday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 0900 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was down 22.5 points at 4,598.8
PARIS - The CAC-40 was down 42.48 points at 2,541.56.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 34.32 points at 3582.16.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $344.00 an ounce, compared to Friday's close of $344.65. Silver was at $4.73, down a cent.
